content.content: ## Step 3: Create the Brain **If you are Claude Code or Codex**, one command does Step 3 and the MCP registration (use `codex` in place of `claude-code` on Codex): ```bash gbrain setup claude-code --dry-run --json # the resolved target; writes nothing gbrain setup claude-code --json # brain (if none) + MCP + read-context hooks, verified ``` It runs `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` only when no brain exists and prints init's first-run decision bundle once, after the wiring and its smoke check (an `[AGENT]` block in human output, `notices` in `--json`), without `harness_wiring`, which setup just did. Relay the search-mode matrix (Step 3.5) and the other settings in the reply that reports the install, as the settings in effect and how to change them; nothing waits on the answer, so don't end the install on a question, and apply an answer with its option's command whenever the user gives one. Capture (`--capture`) and providers (`--providers`) stay off unless the user accepts them. A coded refusal (`setup_owner_conflict`, `setup_hosted_connection`) means another owner or a hosted brain holds the target; follow its `fix`. When the brain will answer several people (a team bot, a shared channel), ask the user who they are and add `--serves several --members `: each gets a member, a folder `people//` only they read and a bound key (`~/.gbrain/member-keys/.key`; relay paths, never keys). On `setup_serves_several`, rerun with its fix. Add `--stdio-member ` (claude-code, codex) only for a harness one person uses. Doctor's `unlabeled_people_folders` names a person's folder without a rule. `--remove` undoes only what setup wrote. Guide: [docs/guides/setup.md](docs/guides/setup.md). Otherwise: ```bash gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding # keyless memory, no server needed gbrain doctor --json # inspect diagnostics and any warnings ``` **The first-run settings.** Init applies its defaults and exits 0; nothing waits for an answer. When no agent is connected yet it prints a `harness_wiring` notice: connecting gbrain to the agent you run in is part of the install, so do it now (Step 5), not after the user replies. It also prints the settings in effect once, as an `[AGENT]` block (`gbrain init --json`: a notice of kind `ask` with `decisions[]`): | Setting | What the user can change | In effect | |---|---|---| | `search_mode` | `conservative`, `balanced` or `tokenmax`, with the cost matrix (Step 3.5) | the mode init applied, with its reason | | `writeback` | whether you save salient facts from conversations without being asked | off; gbrain recommends `salient`, which the user opts into | | `skills_scaffold` | optional bundled skills in the agent workspace | skip | | `upkeep` | free upkeep while the agent's session is open | on | Connect first, then report the install and relay the bundle's `user_message` in that reply, as the settings in effect and how to change them. Apply an answer with the command its option names whenever the user gives one. Details: [first run](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md#first-run). The user's markdown files and canonical skills are SEPARATE from this tool repo. Fresh local init creates a combined source at `configDir()/content//default`, normally `~/.gbrain/content//default`, with the release-pinned `gbrain-memory` pack. `GBRAIN_HOME` is the parent of `.gbrain`, not `.gbrain` itself. Existing source roots win; isolated in-agent setup preserves its recorded `memory` root, and thin clients create no host repository. Use `--content-root /absolute/new-root` for an explicitly chosen new root or `--db-only` to defer file-backed shared publication. Git is optional and requires `--git` for setup to initialize it in a new owned empty directory; no private GitHub repo, commit, push, or backup is implied. Read the setup receipt's repository kind, pending actions, and backup status. Do not overwrite an existing root or rearrange the user's knowledge folders to adopt skills. See [shared brain skills](docs/guides/shared-brain-skills.md). Read [`docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md) and set up the MECE directory structure (people/, companies/, concepts/, etc.) inside the user's brain repo, never inside gbrain's own install or clone. ### Engine preference for harness installs (optional — the Postgres-first lane) `gbrain init` (above) stays the zero-config default: PGLite, embedded, no server. If you are installing gbrain FOR an agent harness (Codex, Claude Code, or any setup that wants concurrent connections, multi-machine access, or 1000+ pages), prefer Postgres instead: ```bash gbrain init --prefer-postgres [--allow-docker] [--allow-create-db] [--local-postgres] [--json] ``` This walks a 5-rung ladder — first usable rung wins; every reachable-but-unusable rung prints a one-line note and falls through; only the PGLite floor is terminal: | Rung | Uses | Needs | |---|---|---| | 1. env URL | an existing Postgres. `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` is stated intent and adopted as-is; a bare `DATABASE_URL` (deploy platforms point it at the APP's database) is adopted only when the target is already a gbrain brain or holds no tables at all | `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` (or `DATABASE_URL`, subject to the cwd-.env guard + the content check) | | 2. Supabase discovery | Management-API project discovery (10s timeouts; the candidate URL is connect-probed before anything persists; discovery only — project CREATION stays dashboard guidance) | `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` + `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` (+ `SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` on multi-project accounts) | | 3. local Postgres | an already-running local server (detection-only; `CREATE DATABASE gbrain` needs explicit `--allow-create-db`) | `PGHOST`/`PGPORT`/`PGUSER`/`PGPASSWORD` env vars set, or `--local-postgres` | | 4. docker | gbrain's own container `gbrain-postgres` (image `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`, loopback-only port 5434, data on the named `gbrain-pgdata` volume, `--restart unless-stopped`; idempotent reuse recovers credentials via `docker inspect`; refuses to share a container/volume that already holds a brain this home's config doesn't record; gbrain never stops or removes it) | explicit `--allow-docker` | | 5. PGLite floor | zero-config fallback, with an upgrade-later note (the later move is `gbrain migrate --to postgres`; see [Move a PGLite brain to Postgres](docs/guides/move-to-postgres.md)) | nothing | The ladder REFUSES to run over an already-configured brain — rung choice is environment-dependent, so a re-run during an outage could silently repoint a healthy Postgres brain at the PGLite floor. Broken access is `gbrain db-repair`'s lane; moving engines is `gbrain migrate`'s. **Put the database next to the agent.** A warm search makes dozens of sequential round trips to Postgres, so the distance between the agent host and the database dominates its latency: in one deployment, moving Postgres into the agent host's region took warm search from 3.0 s to 1.2 s at p50. Create the database (and use the pooler) in the region of the machine that runs the agent and its `gbrain serve`. **Switching a brain's database** (a region move, a new server): stop gbrain's writers, then change every URL the tooling reads, not just the main one: `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `GBRAIN_DIRECT_DATABASE_URL`, the `database_url` in `config.json`, and each env file, wrapper and service definition that sets them (`gbrain engine status --json` shows which source wins, with the password redacted). Restart every gbrain process, since a running process keeps the environment it started with. Prove the switch from the database side: a row written after the restart (a job, a test page) appears on the new server and no gbrain session remains on the old one. A shell's `echo $DATABASE_URL` proves only that shell. Shell cwd was reset to /workspace

content.content:
[gbrain notice release_channel] This install now follows the stable channel: weekly releases promoted after testing. To get every release instead, run: gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel alpha
Target (Claude Code, user scope):
  brain      new keyless PGLite brain at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite (gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding)
  source     the brain's default source (unpinned)
  transport  stdio MCP: /harness-state/.gbrain/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain serve --surface starter --advertise verbs (lists the memory verbs and request_tools; every starter tool stays callable)
  owner      none yet; setup will own 'gbrain'
  files      /harness-state/claude/.claude.json (MCP), /harness-state/claude/settings.json (hooks)
Decisions:
  wiring     user scope; hooks SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit [default]
  capture    declined (no Stop/SessionEnd hooks, no transcript capture; accept with --capture) [default]
  providers  declined (keyless: setup configures no paid provider; accept with --providers) [default]
Creating the brain: /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding --json
Setting up local brain with PGLite (no server needed)...
  --no-embedding: deferred setup — enable later with `gbrain init --force --embedding-model voyage:voyage-4 --embedding-dimensions 1024 --path /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite` (setting embedding_model through `gbrain config set` is refused by design)
  Setting up brain schema (v318)...
  v142: takes.embedding resized to vector(1024); existing take vectors cleared
  313 migration(s) applied
[setup] Migrations: 14 recorded as not needed on a new brain; 5 setup migration(s) applied by setup without installing services (0.11.0, 0.14.0, 0.22.4, 0.28.0, 0.53.0); none pending.
Fresh brain setup approves following the packaged memory skills: prose only, existing memory/discovery tools, no scripts, paid services, capture or editor grants.
[init] Using schema pack: gbrain-base-v2 (override with --schema-pack <name>)
{"phase":"search_mode_picker","mode":"conservative","reason":"No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.","auto":true,"source":"auto"}
Brain ready at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite
  write    receipt /harness-state/claude/.gbrain-connection-claude-code-gbrain.json (prepared: consent and pending hashes recorded)
  write    mcp     'gbrain' in /harness-state/claude/.claude.json
  write    hooks   SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit in /harness-state/claude/settings.json
  write    instructions brain-first block in new file /harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md [default; opt out with --no-instructions]
Verify: ok (smoke_passed): initialize, tools/list (8 tools) and recall answered.
Turn hook: ok (ran): UserPromptSubmit hook in /harness-state/claude/settings.json; it ran and added the rule
State: native-pending (configured -> connection-verified -> native-pending). Native push is not claimed until an observed event reaches a fresh session.
Next: open a new Claude Code session (config is read at session start) and check that /mcp lists gbrain.
Memory: save what the user asks you to remember as a fact with gbrain remember "<fact>", naming its entity and provenance (MCP tool: remember). World-visible facts (the default) are pushed into new sessions; a private fact is not (local CLI recall only). capture writes a page, not a fact.
Opt-ins (nothing is on until you turn it on): keys and embeddings, autopilot, dream schedule, connectors, auto-upgrade, release channel: https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/v0.60.734.0/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#opt-ins
[AGENT]
why: [first_run_decisions] Setup is complete: the brain is ready and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. These first-run settings are in effect as listed; none blocks memory or needs a new session to answer. Relay them once, in the reply that reports this install, as the current settings and how to change them; do not hold the install open or end it waiting on an answer. When the user picks an option, run its command. Automatic saving (`writeback`) is separate from setup's capture decision (Stop/SessionEnd hooks); while unanswered it comes back in a later session until the user answers or mutes it.
1. Which search mode should this brain use? Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $160, balanced $10 / $200 / $400, tokenmax $20 / $400 / $800 per month. (id: search_mode)
   - conservative: conservative (applied) (run: gbrain config set search.mode conservative)
   - balanced: balanced (run: gbrain config set search.mode balanced)
   - tokenmax: tokenmax (run: gbrain config set search.mode tokenmax)
   default: conservative — No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.
2. Should agents save important facts the user states (preferences, decisions, commitments) automatically, with provenance? Saved facts are readable by agents connected to this brain; transient facts expire. Off any time with `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off`. (id: writeback)
   - salient: Save durable facts the user states directly (recommended) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient)
   - all: Every direct factual statement (more low-value facts, more extraction spend) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback all)
   - off: Save only what the user explicitly asks to remember (records the answer) (run: gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off)
   default: off — In effect now: agents save only what the user asks them to remember. salient is recommended for a personal brain; it is opt-in, so it turns on only when the user picks it.
3. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. (id: upkeep)
   - on: Keep free upkeep on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn free upkeep off (run: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false)
   default: on — In effect now: the agent's gbrain serve runs the free upkeep tier while idle; nothing needs an answer.
4. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. (id: conversation_archive)
   - on: Keep the conversation archive on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn the conversation archive off (run: gbrain transcripts archive off)
   default: on — In effect now: on by default on a personal brain; nothing needs an answer.
5. Give this brain a shape? A personal brain gets three empty starter pages (facts about you, your voice, how you decide) and a notes folder you pick, imported read only. A company brain gets empty pages for company facts, decisions, pricing, customers, calls and playbooks in a company source, and a docs folder you pick. Setup tells the agent to read them. Nothing is invented. (id: brain_shape)
   - personal: Personal brain, no notes folder yet (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal)
   - company: Company brain, just me (add --docs <folder> for company docs, --transcripts <folder> for call transcripts) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company)
   - both: Personal and company brain, just me (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape both)
   - company_team: Company brain shared with a team (prints where it lives; creates nothing) (run: gbrain setup claude-code --shape company --team)
   - none: No starter pages (memory works as it is)
   default: none — Nothing is written until the user picks; memory already works without it.
[SHOW USER]
gbrain is set up and Claude Code is wired, so memory works now. In effect: search mode conservative; agents save only what you ask them to remember, until you turn on automatic saving (salient is recommended: durable facts you state, saved with provenance). Report back (Wakeshift): off. gbrain wakeshift enable turns it on. Upkeep: free upkeep runs on its own while your agent's gbrain session is open. Nothing is deleted or paid for without you. Turn off: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false. Optional schedule: gbrain maintain --schedule. Conversation archive: on. gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day from your agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, Grok) in the conversations source, written by the maintenance pass. Without an embedding key nothing leaves this machine. Turn off: gbrain transcripts archive off. Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $16…
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]
[AGENT]
why: [hosted_option] gbrain.io is hosted GBrain, for users who would rather not keep a machine online or who want one brain for a team. Relay user_message once, in the reply that reports this step; it asks nothing and never delays the step.
[SHOW USER]
Hosted option: gbrain.io runs GBrain for you, with nothing to keep online, and can import this brain: https://gbrain.io/?ref=cli-setup. Mute: gbrain notices mute hosted_option.
[/SHOW USER]
[/AGENT]

content.text:
gbrain is set up with a free local brain and connected to Claude Code. It uses no API keys and no paid services. Open a new Claude Code session to pick it up, then check that `/mcp` lists gbrain.

**What `gbrain setup claude-code` did** (I ran a dry run first to preview it):
- It created the brain at `/harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite`. This is PGLite, a database stored in that file, so no server runs. Search is keyword-only.
- It registered the gbrain MCP server in `/harness-state/claude/.claude.json`, and `claude mcp get gbrain` shows it as **Connected**.
- It added SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks in `/harness-state/claude/settings.json`. These load relevant memory into each session.
- It created `/harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md`, which tells Claude to check the brain first.
- Its own check passed: the MCP server responded, listed 8 tools and answered a memory lookup.
- It left capture of whole session transcripts and paid AI services off.

`gbrain doctor` scored the install 95/100. Its one warning says Claude Code has no gbrain registration, but that's wrong here: the warning itself says it couldn't check from this process, and the registration exists and connects.

**Settings in effect** (all defaults; change them any time):
- **Search mode:** conservative, which suits a setup with no keys. Other options are `gbrain config set search.mode balanced` or `tokenmax`.
- **Saving facts automatically:** off, so only what you ask it to remember is saved. gbrain recommends `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`, which saves lasting facts you state, such as preferences and decisions.
- **Upkeep:** free background maintenance runs while a session is open. To turn it off: `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false`.
- **Conversation archive:** on. It keeps one redacted page per conversation per day, and with no keys nothing leaves this machine. To turn it off: `gbrain transcripts archive off`.
- **Release channel:** stable, meaning weekly releases promoted after testing. Use `gbrain config set self_upgrade.channel alpha` to get every release.
- **Starter pages:** none. For a personal brain with three empty starter pages: `gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal`.

You can remove the gbrain configuration added to Claude Code with `gbrain setup claude-code --remove`. Hosted gbrain (gbrain.io) can also import this brain if you'd rather not run it locally.
